# Architecture Specification: Bookstore Application

## System Architecture

### Component Diagram
```mermaid
graph TD
    Client[Next.js Frontend] --> API[FastAPI Backend]
    API --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
    API --> Cache[Redis Cache]
    API --> Auth[JWT Auth]
```

## Technology Stack
| Component | Technology | Rationale |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Backend | FastAPI 0.104+ | Async support, auto OpenAPI docs, Pydantic validation |
| Frontend | Next.js 14 (App Router) | SSR, React Server Components, file-based routing |
| Database | PostgreSQL 15 | ACID compliance, full-text search, JSON support |
| ORM | SQLAlchemy 2.0 | Async support, type-safe queries |
| Auth | JWT + bcrypt | Stateless, scalable authentication |
| Cache | Redis | Session cache, search result cache |
| CSS | Tailwind CSS | Utility-first, responsive design |

## API Contracts

### Books
- `GET /api/books` — List books with pagination and filtering
- `GET /api/books/{id}` — Get book by ID
- `POST /api/books` — Create book (admin only)
- `PUT /api/books/{id}` — Update book (admin only)
- `DELETE /api/books/{id}` — Delete book (admin only)
- `GET /api/books/search?q={query}` — Full-text search

### Cart
- `GET /api/cart` — Get current user's cart
- `POST /api/cart/items` — Add item to cart
- `DELETE /api/cart/items/{id}` — Remove item from cart

### Orders
- `POST /api/orders` — Create order from cart
- `GET /api/orders` — List user's orders
- `GET /api/orders/{id}` — Get order details

### Auth
- `POST /api/auth/register` — Register new user
- `POST /api/auth/login` — Login and get JWT
- `GET /api/auth/me` — Get current user profile

## Authentication Model
- JWT tokens with 24h expiry
- Refresh tokens stored in httpOnly cookies
- Role-based access: `customer`, `admin`
- bcrypt password hashing with salt rounds = 12

## ADR-001: FastAPI over Django
- **Decision:** Use FastAPI
- **Rationale:** Async-first, automatic OpenAPI, Pydantic validation built-in
- **Trade-off:** Less batteries-included than Django, need manual admin panel

## ADR-002: PostgreSQL Full-Text Search over Elasticsearch
- **Decision:** Use PostgreSQL tsvector + GIN indexes
- **Rationale:** Simpler infrastructure, sufficient for bookstore scale
- **Trade-off:** Less advanced features than Elasticsearch
